title: An illustration Ask draws looks illustrated: natural shapes, light and shadow, depth
goal: When a person asks for an illustration (a sun over mountains, a landscape, an animal), Ask draws it the way an illustrator would: natural outlines instead of plain triangles and circles, a light side and a shadow side that agree with where the light comes from, soft gradients, and depth from layers that fade into the distance. An icon request stays simple and bold; an illustration request gets the craft.

I think if you're drawing an svg illustration of sun over mountains it should be more elaborate.' Those are other people's paid or licensed artwork: study the techniques, never trace, copy or ship any of them. Masks and clipping exist in the app (a layer used as a mask); check the agent tools reach them.

The user, 2026-10-20: 'consider how would a graphic artist break down these concepts'. The eight passes in the acceptance are that breakdown. Each pass is also a place to measure: values in grey from the render, the thumbnail and silhouette tests as the judge seeing a 32 point and a solid black copy, light agreement by checking each shadow face is on the side away from the sun. Small local models do much better at one narrow step at a time than at one prompt for the whole picture, so passes should help the model as well as the result; measure it with the eval.
acceptance: 'draw an svg illustration of a sun over mountains' on a blank picture gives mountains with irregular ridgelines and curves (no straight-sided triangles), each with a lit face and a shadow face that agree with where the sun is, at least three ranges that get lighter and bluer into the distance, a sky gradient, and nothing poking past the picture by accident (the user's result had a stray green wedge off the right edge)

The quality bar is the user's reference board (queue/audits/2026-10-20-user-sun-mountains-reference-board.png): before building, the runner studies how those pieces are made and writes the techniques into the audit, at least: silhouettes with snow and ridge highlights cut as negative space, sun rays as an even radial burst, a scene clipped into a circle or badge with a frame line, repeated pine silhouettes for a treeline, lake reflections as stacked horizontal strokes, and layered sunset ridges stepping in value under a gradient sky

Ask follows the style the person names: 'line art', 'silhouette', 'badge' or 'circle', 'sunset', 'flat' each give that look, and with no style named it picks one and the row says which. The eval gets one case per style (sun over mountains as line art, as a black silhouette badge with pines, as a layered sunset), each scoring 7 or more on crafted and designed, and a judge shown the board says the result belongs among them

Ask draws the way a graphic artist works, in passes, each its own step with an output that can be checked before the next: (1) brief: subject, style, use (icon, badge, poster), mood and time of day; (2) composition: the frame, a focal point off centre, the horizon off the middle, overlaps for depth, a blocking of the big shapes as boxes; (3) values before colour: three to five value planes, nearest darkest (or lightest at night), checked so the picture reads in grey; (4) shape language: big, then medium, then small; peaks lopsided with uneven slopes and broken ridgelines, trees one simplified shape repeated at varied sizes; (5) light: one light direction from the sun, every form split into a lit side and a shadow side along its ridge, highlights cut as negative space, cast shadows agreeing; (6) colour: a palette of three to five hues in one harmony, distance lighter, bluer and lower in contrast, a sky gradient; (7) detail and finish: detail densest at the focal point, a line weight order for line art (outline heaviest), clean joins, nothing clipped by accident; (8) critique: squint test, thumbnail test at 32 points, silhouette test in solid black, then revise what fails. The audit shows one picture per pass for the sun over mountains

Techniques become reusable pieces Ask can call (for example a treeline, a ray burst, a ridge with a shadow face, a clip to a circle), so a drawing is composed rather than written point by point; which ones is the runner's call, logged

The eval's rubric gets a 'crafted' line for illustrations (natural forms, light and shadow, depth, finish), and the user's picture (queue/audits/2026-10-20-user-ask-sun-over-mountains.png) scores 3 or lower on it

Five illustration cases in the eval (sun over mountains, a forest at dusk, a lighthouse on a cliff, a fox, a city skyline at night) reach 7 or more on crafted and designed for Ask on this Mac, before and after in the audit; the thirteen drawing cases of the dog task do not go down
Every part stays editable and named (ridges, shadow faces, sky, sun), uses the app's own gradient fills, and exports as clean SVG

Audit under queue/audits/ with a contact sheet before and after and the scores. Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note: intake: the user's reference board sets the quality bar; styles by name; techniques as reusable pieces
intake: draw in a graphic artist's eight passes, each checkable

from ask-draws-a-dog (2026-10-20): Ask now draws a thing with ONE add_drawing call (built-in Twemoji set first, else the model's own whole SVG, read into editable layers by SVGArtwork) and looks at it with llama3.2-vision before handing back, redrawing at most twice (AskDrawingCheck, AskSession.look). Off the set, qwen3:30b's own SVGs are the weak spot: a lighthouse was seen as 'a square', 'pencil sharpener', 'matchstick' and a windmill as 'a red rectangle', 'a stick figure', 'a bow tie' over three tries each, then Ask gave up (run 20261020-185749-ask, temporary cases zz-lighthouse/zz-windmill, not in the history). The look-and-redraw loop is there to reuse; what it needs is better drawing, which is this task.

technique study of the user's board (studied, nothing copied): (1) one-colour silhouettes where snow caps and ridge highlights are NEGATIVE space, white wedges cut down from each peak along the light side; (2) sun rays as an even radial burst of tapered strokes from a half sun on the horizon, gaps equal; (3) the scene clipped into a circle with a heavier frame line, the ground running out flat at the bottom of the circle; (4) treelines from ONE pine silhouette (stacked tiers, trunk) repeated at varied heights, taller at the edges; (5) a lake as stacked horizontal strokes that shorten as they go down (reflection), under the horizon; (6) layered sunset ridges: 4-6 ridge bands stepping in value from pale far to dark near under a vertical gradient sky, sun as a pale disc low behind the far ranges; (7) line art: outline heaviest, interior ridge and shadow hatching lighter.

adversarial review: a small local model writing a whole illustration SVG cannot hold light direction, value order and ridge noise at once (the dog task's lighthouse/windmill failed 3 of 3), so Ask should only make the narrow choices (subject, style words, time of day) and the craft lives in code, built in the eight passes, each a pure function with a checkable output. Grown-up tool check: an Illustrator user expects named groups (Sky, Far ridge, Far ridge shadow, Sun), real gradient fills they can edit, and an SVG that opens cleanly; masks do not export to SVG here, so clipping (badge circle, poster edge) is done in the geometry rather than with a mask.

Chose: extend add_drawing with a style argument (free words: line art, silhouette, badge/circle, sunset, flat, illustration) over a separate add_illustration tool, because the look-and-redraw loop, the undo step and the change row already hang off add_drawing. A scene (mountains, forest, lighthouse, skyline, a named style, the word illustration) goes to the illustration engine; a single thing or an icon stays on the built-in set. SVGArtwork learns real linear and radial gradients so the parts carry the app's own gradient fills.

Chose: the craft in code (Illustrator, eight pure passes with checks, IllustrationPieces) over a better prompt for the model's own svg, because the model's svgs for a lighthouse failed 3 of 3 and the before run made nothing for 4 of 8 scenes. Chose: one light direction for the whole picture (every shadow on the side away from the sun's side) over per-peak shadows, because the judge read per-peak flips as inconsistent twice. Chose: clipping to the badge circle and poster box in the geometry over a mask, because masks do not export to SVG. Chose: Ask's blind look skips illustrations and built-in drawings, because a misread built-in tree ('a mushroom') was swapped for the model's green blob (judge 3.5).

Bug found and fixed on the way: RGBA.relativeLuminance is not linearised, so value studies use IllustrationColor.value (CIE L*).
